eid_r.declaration: EvE has no native evaluator identity (native_scheme=none): the evaluator is whichever shell step evaluation.steps names, and EvE hands that step exactly EVE_WORKSPACE_ROOT, EVE_SOLVER_ROOT, EVE_EVAL_LOG_ROOT and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and no evaluator parameters (workflow/evaluation.py:290-318). The adapter pins EID* by overriding evaluation.steps with a generated step that invokes the frozen E* by absolute path and writes EID* and PINS_SHA256 into the log root it is handed. EID_r.value = 'sha256:' + sha256("a0/eve/eid_r/v1" || 0x00 || canonical_json(payload)) with payload = {schema, eid_star, native_scheme, mapping_mode, evaluator_source{digest,files}, fr_spec_hash}: eid_star is an argument of the hash, so a different EID* necessarily gives a different EID_r. Recompute from the published inputs alone with runtimes/eve/tools/recompute-eid-r (recipe: eid_r.derivation in the conformance document).

derivation.algorithm: value = 'sha256:' + sha256("a0/eve/eid_r/v1" || 0x00 || canonical_json(payload)); canonical_json = json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False) encoded ascii (a0/contract/evalcontract.py::canonical_json)

inputs_source.eid_star: eid_star field of the EID* document
inputs_source.evaluator_source: components.EvaluatorSource of the EID* document, re-hashed from a0/tasks/circle-packing/{e_star.py,e_star_child.py} and compared before use

injected_step.note: provenance, deliberately NOT hashed into EID_r: the rendered step embeds the run's absolute state-dir path, so including it would make EID_r a per-run-directory value rather than an evaluator identity. The step is what A0.1 exercises and what `a01` reports on.

declared.note: E* verdict -> trace failure_stage. The trace schema fixes the enum but not this per-runtime mapping; SimpleLoop freezes it here and reports it to the contract owner so the other runtimes can adopt the same one.

failure_stage_accounting_basis.extension: rows whose E* verdict is `ok` but whose runtime attempt failed anyway are staged evaluator_failed and counted in a01.failure_stage_extension — declared, not silent; 0 such rows in this run
failure_stage_accounting_basis.staging_rule: every C* row: failure_stage = table(E* status, E* failure.kind); the same value is written to the trace event and to the row, so check (c) of §4.5 cannot drift

failure_stage_counts_scope: this subcommand writes the A0.1 trace only, so the counts are exactly the 14 C* rows (`a01.failure_stage_counts`), staged with the adopted frozen A0-wide table and equal to the frozen map over C*'s E* verdicts: {none: 5, verify_failed: 5, resolve_failed: 1, evaluator_failed: 2, timeout: 1}
